subject: TideBank discovery — inference unit economics & next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@tidebank.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: TideBank discovery — inference unit economics & next steps

Hi Sara / Ryan,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next actions. TL;DR: primary ask is to materially reduce inference unit economics while preserving current latency/quality targets; TideBank is open to batching/caching and modest quantization if we validate quality.

Key pain points (what you told us):
- Unit cost for customer-facing features is ~3-4x what product targets support (esp. auth/notification journeys).
- Current infra: self-hosted fleet (K8s) running an open 7B model on mixed T4 / A10g nodes; cache is mostly at the app layer (no KV cache for KV-attention reuse).
- Burst traffic during payroll/statement windows causes CPU queueing; P95 latency spikes are the main customer complaint.
- Procurement and security constraints mean you prefer a private deployment or a dedicated pool rather than multi-tenant hosted.

Success criteria for a pilot / evaluation (agreed):
1) Per-token inference cost reduced by >= 2.5–3x for the targeted flows (auth/email templates, fraud scoring).
2) P95 generation latency < 100ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) under steady-state load.
3) Zero production-quality regressions vs. current model (we will run your prompt set + hidden evals).
4) Clear operational plan for rollout (monitoring, canary, fallback).

What Redwood can help with / what we proposed on the call:
- Pilot options: dedicated reserved capacity (on-prem VPC or dedicated cloud pool) vs. hosted dedicated with private tenancy.
- Optimization levers: continuous batching, KV prefix caching, quantization profiles (4-bit/FP16 tradeoffs), and model variant recommendations for cost/latency balance.
- Instrumentation: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, and prompt-level regression checks.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
- Sara: send a 48–72h sample of representative traces (API logs + 10–20 example prompt/response pairs) — needed to size batching and kv/cache benefit (due by Tue 2/23).
- Redwood (Olga + Markus): produce a one-page pilot outline + unit-econ snapshot based on the traces (deliver by Thu 2/25). Attachment: tidebank-pilot-outline.xlsx, unit-econ-snapshot.csv
- Schedule: propose a 30–45m follow-up POC scoping call week of Mar 1 to validate pilot scope and align security requirements.

Risks / open questions:
- Any strict banned libraries or air-gap restrictions for the private deploy?
- Expected monthly token volumes for the pilot flows (rough ballpark is fine).
- Internal owner on TideBank side for security/compliance (we'll loop them into the follow-up).

If this looks right I can draft the pilot outline and send a short pricing band for hosted vs dedicated so you have a ballpark before procurement.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0127

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@tidebank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ryan Patel <ryan@tidebank.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:19:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: TideBank discovery — inference unit economics & next steps

Thanks, Olga — solid recap and we appreciate the clarity. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- We'll share 72 hours of anonymized API traces by EOD Tue (2/23). Included: per-request latency, token counts, and a small set of example prompts/responses (we'll scrub any account identifiers).
- On deployment preference: we strongly prefer a dedicated pool within our cloud tenant (VPC-mode) if the performance/cost delta to on-prem isn't large. We'll need KMS integration and audit-log export as a hard requirement.
- Quantization: team is open to 4-bit quantization experiments as long as you validate zero visible regressions on our safety/sentiment checks.

Two asks for your pilot outline: please include an explicit rollback plan for the canary (we need clear steps for reverting model variants and traffic split). Also include a short paragraph on compliance (SOC2/HIPAA posture) and which artifacts Redwood will provide for procurement.

Finally, can you ballpark an expected per-token cost range for the pilot under the dedicated pool assumption? We understand it will be a range, just want to set expectations for procurement.

We'll be available on Wed (2/24) afternoon if you want to sync briefly — otherwise the week of Mar 1 call works.

—Sara
Head of ML Platform, TideBank
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@tidebank.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: TideBank discovery — inference unit economics & next steps

Hi Sara — quick follow from Redwood on the pricing and pilot commitments. Happy to hop on Wed 2/24 afternoon as well; suggest 30m to confirm scope once we see the traces.

Ballpark per-token ranges (for sizing discussion only):
- Hosted dedicated (Redwood-managed) — expected unit: $0.0009 — $0.0025 per generated token depending on model variant and batching.
- Private/dedicated in-customer-VPC (Redwood control plane) — expected unit: $0.0007 — $0.0020 per generated token (savings from colocated infra + tailored batching).
- Typical savings from aggressive batching + KV prefix caching: 20% - 45% relative to naive single-request serving (depends on prompt shape and reuse).
- Additional quantization benefit (4-bit) we often see: incremental 15% - 35% cost reduction but requires the eval pass you mentioned to ensure no quality regression.

What we'll include in the pilot outline (deliverable by Thu 2/25):
- Pilot objectives, success criteria (mapped to the items Olga listed), and timeline.
- Concrete canary/rollback steps (traffic split, health checks, auto-fallback).
- Compliance artifacts we can provide: SOC2 attachable report, audit-log export examples, KMS integration notes.
- Measurement plan: token-level cost dashboard, prompt/regression suite results, and per-route latency SLO checks.

I've also linked a starter pilot doc and the HubSpot deal record here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cPilotOutline (pilot outline) and https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4782 (deal).

If you'd rather we provide a narrower per-token estimate after we analyze the traces, we can do that — the ranges above are intentionally conservative until we size memory/throughput needs from your traces.

Looking forward to the trace data.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
